findings.reasoning: Step 1: The code sets the CORS header "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" to "*", which allows any origin to access the resources. This wildcard configuration is a security misconfiguration because it removes origin restrictions, potentially exposing the API to cross-site request forgery (CSRF) and other cross-origin attacks. The presence of "Access-Control-Allow-Credentials" set to "true" further amplifies the risk by allowing credentials to be sent from any origin, which can lead to credential leakage or unauthorized access.
findings.description: Wildcard CORS header with credentials enabled exposes the API to cross-origin attacks and credential leakage.
